payout_quote: NCUA: 'If you believe the NCUA may be holding funds for you, please review our current list of unclaimed deposits.' Step 1: 'Confirm your credit union was liquidated by the NCUA' via its list of involuntary liquidations. This finds YOUR OWN share-account money from a liquidated credit union if it exists — it never promises anyone has any.
timing: Reviewing the list is instant. Claims go through the Member Verification Form sent to NCUA's Asset Management and Assistance Center (mail or amacmail@ncua.gov); timing is per-case.
biggest_catch: Only applies if YOUR credit union was liquidated by the NCUA — step 1 of the official process. And the 18-month clock matters: shares claimed within 18 months of liquidation are paid at full insured amount; after that they are considered uninsured and paid only pro-rata from whatever funds remain.
eligibility: Members of federally insured credit unions that were involuntarily liquidated. The published list shows last names and first initials; you confirm identity via the Member Verification Form.
steps: Go to https://ncua.gov/support-services/conservatorships-liquidations/unclaimed-deposits and confirm your credit union appears on NCUA's list of involuntary liquidations.
Review the current list of unclaimed deposits (last names + first initials) for your name.
If listed, complete the Member Verification Form with as much account information as you can provide.
Send the form to NCUA's Asset Management and Assistance Center — by mail (10910 Domain Drive, Suite 200, Austin, TX 78758) or email (amacmail@ncua.gov) — and await their verification.
catches: Only covers liquidated federally insured credit unions — almost nobody will have a match.
The 18-month insurance window is the key catch: claim late and shares are uninsured, paid only pro-rata from remaining funds.
In some cases funds are transferred to the state's unclaimed-property section instead — then R0296 (state search) is the path.
The public list shows only last names and first initials, so you must verify identity through the form.
notes: Verified 2026-09-22/23: the NCUA unclaimed-deposits page is current (crawled within a day) with the 3-step process and the unclaimed-deposits dataset is public on catalog.data.gov (updated Feb 2025, catalog checked Sept 2026). In-app, this route must lead with the 18-month warning and the liquidated-credit-union prerequisite. No app — website/mail/email only.
